body: I have a similar issue with the router, all lazy-loaded routes cause an endless loop, my issue has nothing to do with guards, I even turned them off, the problem still persists

Hi @chris13524, can you try to update your guard to return a `UrlTree` instead of combining `false` and `navigate`? In general, if you want your guard to redirect, that's the way I would recommend doing it (the feature was added in v8 I believe).
@atscott Yes, that seems to avoid this issue.
Great, glad to hear that worked for you! I'm going to close this issue as it seems to be resolved.
If this is going to be closed, then the example in the documentation should also be updated: https://angular.io/guide/router#canactivate-requiring-authentication
Ah, good catch and agreed. Reopening and adding the docs label to this report.
Guide can't be updated at this time because the last step adds `CanLoad` which doesn't support returning `UrlTree` for a redirect. Blocking issue: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/28306

issue.title: docs(router): Update router guide to use UrlTree for guard redirects

issue.body:
The current implementation for redirecting users inside guards was in place
before the feature was added to allow `CanActivate` and `CanActivateChild` guards
to return `UrlTree` for redirecting users.

Returning `UrlTree` should be the default method, as it provides a more desirable
redirecting experience. When using `router.navigate` followed by `return false`,
the `Router` calls `resetUrlToCurrentUrlTree` (in the `finalize` operator) before
processing the navigation to the new route.  This can result in an undesirable
history if the navigation was the first navigation in the application - that is,
the route will briefly be reset to just `/` (see #36187).

Fixes #36187

Note: This PR targets master only because returning `UrlTree` is a feature that is only available to `CanActivateChild` guards in v10 (#36610).
